title: NeuroEdge Gated Tool Profile — ToolCall envelope v1
description: The tool-call envelope of the Gated Tool Profile (docs/spec/tool_calling.md §1) and the tool description `tools/list` returns. `#/$defs/request` is what a caller sends; `#/$defs/call` is the envelope the dispatcher holds, the data of the `tool_call` trace event. A passing validation proves the envelope's shape only: whether the tool exists, whether the arguments fit its inputSchema after coercion, and the gate's limits are decided by the runtime (the corpus fixtures/tool_calls/ is the conformance test).

id.description: Assigned by the provider. Empty or absent: the dispatcher numbers it call_1, call_2…

name.description: The tool's name. An unknown name is a REJECTED result at dispatch, not an envelope error.

arguments.description: The call's arguments. Their types are the tool's `inputSchema`, not the envelope's. The key `__unparseable__` is reserved: the runtime puts it here when a provider's arguments were not valid JSON, and dispatch rejects the call.

source.description: Where the call came from. Assigned by the runtime — from the connection, a bridge's registration or the verified client — never the caller's to state (tool_calling.md §5). A built-in name, or `bridge:<id>` / `mcp:<client>`.

request.description: What a caller sends. It carries no `source`: a request that states one is refused at the envelope.

call.description: The envelope the dispatcher holds: a request plus the source it assigned.

input_schema.description: The JSON Schema subset a tool's `inputSchema` is written in: an object of scalar parameters. `minimum`, `maximum`, `enum` and `maxLength` come from the gate's `arguments` limits and are a hint to the caller: a value outside them is the gate's BLOCK `argument_out_of_range`, not a REJECTED.

tool.description: One entry of `tools/list`. `outputSchema` is tool-result.v1.json with `properties.tool` pinned to `name`.
